chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Abdullah, from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abul Jarud who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Qaim will rule for three hundred and nine years, just as the people of the Cave remained in their cave. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, as it was filled with injustice and tyranny. Allah will open for him the east and west of the earth, and he will kill the people until no religion remains except that of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). He will proceed with the way of Sulaiman ibn Dawud... The rest of the report.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.تَمَامُ الْخَبَرِ: The rest of the report, a closing phrase indicating the narration is complete
key_terms.ثَلَاثَمِائَةٍ وَتِسْعَ سِنِينَ: Three hundred and nine years, the specified duration of the Qaim's rule
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ: Sulaiman ibn Dawud (Solomon son of David), whose way the Qaim will follow
key_terms.عَدْلًا وَقِسْطًا: Justice and equity, the state the earth will be filled with under the Qaim

ai.seo_question: How long will the Mahdi rule and what are his key characteristics according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the longevity of the Qaim’s reign as 309 years, drawing a direct parallel to the sleepers of the Cave (Ahl al-Kahf) to signify a divinely preserved era of stability. It emphasizes the universal expansion of his authority ('east and west') and his adherence to the political and spiritual model of Prophet Sulaiman, ensuring the consolidation of pure monotheism through both justice and decisive action.
